assessment: The review describes coffee as a caffeine source and mentions fatigue generally. No independent brewed-coffee fatigue outcome in Parkinson disease.

assessment: The isolated caffeine comparison measures power in mouse hindlimb and diaphragm muscles. The discussion proposes transfer to fatigue resistance, which is not the measured human symptom.

assessment: The iRBD cohort underwent an aggregate clinical smell test that included cinnamon. It reports no cinnamon-specific diagnostic result or change after ground cinnamon intake.

fit: one-time cinnamon odor and separately measured baseline constipation
assessment: Cinnamon appears as a smell test stimulus. Constipation was classified separately at baseline with no exposure or consumption contrast.

fit: cinnamon odor testing and separate sleep disorder assessment
assessment: Cinnamon is named among diagnostic odor items. The cohort enrolled people with iRBD and recorded sleep-related measures independently of the odor. No dream-enactment outcome is attributed to cinnamon.

fit: isolated caffeine, perceived fatigue and vigor measured separately
assessment: The 12-person crossover in healthy older adults reports no clear caffeine effect on the BRUMS fatigue subscale or on exertion, with better vigor. No coffee was administered.

fit: functional and perceived effort outcomes distinct from fatigue
assessment: The 19-person caffeine crossover reports improvement in selected timed tasks and within-visit readiness to invest mental effort. The results do not provide a validated fatigue-severity contrast. Participant linkage with the prior older-adult study is unresolved.

fit: opposite isolated muscle endurance results by activation
assessment: Endurance fell 17.6% with maximal stimulation and increased 19.2% with submaximal stimulation. The concentration, tissue, outcome and route do not estimate brewed coffee or clinical fatigue.
The lower physiological caffeine concentration gave inconclusive changes in recovery force or net power. The much higher exposure had different power effects in the two isolated muscles.

The documented customary uses include perfume and skin hydration, outside a ground-spice pain experiment. Recorded mentions are not symptomatic observations.

fit: two distinct ginger species in cosmetic documentation
